invoicing.navigation.invoices.label: Invoices
invoicing.navigation.series.label: Invoice numbering
invoicing.navigation.exports.label: Exports
invoicing.screens.exports.help: The ledger as another set of books takes it, such as the students' union's return. Every line of every sealed posting in the range goes out once, under the profile's codes.
invoicing.screens.exports.no-profiles-he: A profile says how the file is laid out and which code each ledger account goes out under.
invoicing.screens.exports.open-help: Some of these days are in a period that is not closed, so the file may change if you take it again.
invoicing.screens.exports.too-many: {n} lines is more than one export takes ({max}). Choose a shorter range, such as one period at a time.
invoicing.screens.exports.unmapped: {n} lines have no code in this profile and will go out as unmapped.
invoicing.screens.exports.unmapped.one: 1 line has no code in this profile and will go out as unmapped.
invoicing.screens.exports.same-as: The same file as the one taken on {when}.
invoicing.screens.exports.no-runs: Nothing has been exported with this profile yet.
invoicing.screens.exports.check: Check it would be the same file
invoicing.screens.exports.check-same: Taking this range again gives the same file.
invoicing.screens.exports.check-differs: Taking this range again would give a different file.
invoicing.screens.exports.map-changed: The profile or its codes have changed since.
invoicing.screens.exports.ledger-changed: The ledger for these days has changed since, so a period was open or has been reopened.
invoicing.screens.profiles.help: Each profile lays the ledger out for one set of books and maps every ledger account to that book's code.
invoicing.screens.profiles.none-help: Start from a journal any accounting package takes, or from the students' union return.
invoicing.screens.profiles.starters.jour: Date, journal, account code and name, description, debit, credit, currency, production and source: a layout any accounting package can import.
invoicing.screens.profiles.starters.unio: The old system's union export: date, category, tender, nominal code and the amount in pence and pounds first, then what traces each line, with the money total last.
invoicing.screens.profiles.name: Name
invoicing.screens.profile.help: How the file is laid out, and which code each ledger account goes out under.
invoicing.screens.profile.format-help.jo: A fixed layout: date, journal, account code and name, description, debit and credit (or one amount), currency, production and source.
invoicing.screens.profile.format-help.cu: The columns you choose below, in your order and under your headings.
invoicing.screens.profile.granularity.en: One line for every ledger entry
invoicing.screens.profile.granularity.da: One line per account per day
invoicing.screens.profile.split-by.sourc: What it came from (box office, bar)
invoicing.screens.profile.signs.credit: One amount, credits positive (sales read positive)
invoicing.screens.profile.period-rule-he: The range Exports chooses when this profile is picked. You can change the days before exporting.
invoicing.screens.profile.unmapped-code-: Written on every line whose account has no code, so nothing is silently left out.
invoicing.screens.profile.total-line-hel: A last line adding up the money accounts, money in positive. It is left out of the file's own balance.
invoicing.screens.profile.columns-help: What each column holds, in order, and its heading in the file.
invoicing.screens.profile.columns.code-n: Account name in the other books
invoicing.screens.profile.kind-labels-he: What the Category column says. Give a kind of posting (sale), or a kind and the module or account it is for (sale:bar, sale:box-office.pass-income); the closest match wins.
invoicing.screens.profile.codes-help: The other books' code for each ledger account. A kind of posting can take its own code, such as refunds to a separate nominal code; otherwise the account's code applies. Accounts with entries and no code come first.
invoicing.screens.profile.code-name-for: Name in the other books for {account}
invoicing.screens.profile.code-removed: {account} uses its own code for that kind again
invoicing.screens.profile.kind-add: Add a code for one kind of posting
invoicing.screens.profile.tax-help: The other books' name for each VAT code, written in a package's tax column. The union's return has no tax column, so it can stay empty.
invoicing.screens.profile.preview-help: The start of the file for {range}, {n} lines in all. Nothing is recorded.
invoicing.screens.profile.preview-help.o: The start of the file for {range}, 1 line in all. Nothing is recorded.
invoicing.screens.new.title: New invoice
invoicing.screens.invoices.empty-help: An invoice is for money owed by someone who is not paying at the box office, such as a company hiring a room.
invoicing.screens.draft.name: Name on the invoice
invoicing.screens.draft.name-help: Leave it empty to use their name. A company paying for them goes here.
invoicing.screens.draft.email-help: Where the invoice is sent. For someone with an account, their own address when left empty.
invoicing.screens.draft.reference-help: A purchase order number or anything else they asked to see on it.
invoicing.screens.draft.notes-help: Printed under the lines, such as how to pay.
invoicing.screens.draft.delete-consequen: The draft has no number yet, so nothing is skipped.
invoicing.screens.draft.no-accounts-help: Invoices post to Invoices' own income accounts in Finance. Switch Finance on, then come back.
invoicing.screens.issue.title: Issue
invoicing.screens.issue.help: Issuing gives it the next number and records {amount} owed in the ledger. After that it can only be changed by a credit note.
invoicing.screens.issue.date-help: Today, unless the invoice is for something done earlier.
invoicing.screens.payment.title: Record a payment
invoicing.screens.payment.reference-help: The bank's reference or the cheque number, to find it on a statement.
invoicing.screens.payment.no-accounts-he: Add an Other payment method account under Payments, such as the bank account, then record it.
invoicing.screens.series.help: Each issued invoice takes the next number in its series, so none is skipped or used twice. New invoices use the default series.
invoicing.screens.series.name: Name
invoicing.screens.series.prefix-help: Letters, numbers, hyphens and slashes before the number, such as INV-.
invoicing.screens.series.pad-help: Numbers are padded with noughts to this many digits: 4 gives 0042.
invoicing.screens.issue.send-help: It goes once its PDF is made, usually within a minute.
invoicing.screens.issue.no-email: There is no email address on it, so print the PDF and send it yourself, or add an address before issuing.
invoicing.screens.public.title: Invoice
invoicing.screens.public.heading: Invoice {number} from {theatre}
invoicing.screens.public.not-found: This link does not open an invoice
invoicing.screens.public.not-found-help: It may have expired. Ask whoever sent it to send it again.
invoicing.screens.public.nothing-owed: Nothing to pay: this invoice is settled. Thank you.
invoicing.screens.owed.help: Everyone with an invoice still to pay, most overdue first, with what they owe by how long it has been due.
invoicing.screens.owed.empty: Nobody owes anything on an invoice
invoicing.navigation.owed.label: Owed to us
invoicing.navigation.bills.label: Bills
invoicing.screens.bills.none-waiting: Nothing is waiting for your approval
invoicing.screens.bills.empty-help: Log a supplier's invoice with a copy of it, and someone else approves it before it is paid.
invoicing.screens.bill.number-help: As printed on the supplier's invoice. Needed before the bill is submitted.
invoicing.screens.bill.due-on-help: Left empty, it falls due after the usual payment terms.
invoicing.screens.bill.vat-help: As the supplier's invoice shows it. The rate gives {amount}.
invoicing.screens.bill.vat-differs: The rate gives {worked}; you typed {typed}. Check it against the supplier's invoice.
invoicing.screens.bill.internal-note-hel: Only people who see bills read this.
invoicing.screens.bill.no-accounts: There are no expense accounts to code a bill to
invoicing.screens.bill.no-accounts-help: Add one in Finance's accounts, then come back.
invoicing.screens.bill.file-none: Not attached yet. A bill is submitted only with a copy of the supplier's invoice.
invoicing.screens.bill.approve-consequen: It is posted to the ledger as {amount} owed to the supplier.
invoicing.screens.bill.return-help: It goes back to whoever logged it as a draft, with your reason.
invoicing.screens.bill.waiting-other: You logged this bill, so someone else approves it.
invoicing.screens.bill.delete-consequenc: The draft and its attached invoice are removed.
invoicing.screens.credit.title: Make a credit note
invoicing.screens.credit.help: Up to {amount} of this invoice is left to credit. It is numbered and posted at once, and comes off what is owed; anything already paid stays on the credit note to give back.
invoicing.screens.credit.none: Tick at least one line to credit.
invoicing.screens.write-off.title: Write off
invoicing.screens.write-off.help: {amount} goes to bad debts and the invoice is closed. Only do this when the money will not come.
